title: Loan repayments
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:38Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank points are the present value of an annuity, reducing balance loans and interest factor tables, but none teaches treating a loan as the present value of its repayments and dividing by a present value factor to find the repayment, so this needs a new point.

draft.title: Loan repayments
card: A loan is the present value of all its repayments. It is the amount that, paid in one go today, equals the repayments in value.
So loan = repayment × present value factor. The factor comes from the table, using the interest rate per period and the number of periods.
To find the repayment, divide: repayment = loan ÷ factor. Match the rate to the repayment period, so monthly repayments need a monthly rate.
Example: a $10 000 loan has a factor of 11.2551 for 12 monthly repayments at 1% per month. Repayment = 10 000 ÷ 11.2551 = $888.49.

a.q: Anna borrows $15 000. The table gives a present value factor of 5 for her rate and term. What is each repayment?
a.why: The loan equals repayment × factor, so repayment = 15 000 ÷ 5 = $3000. Multiplying gives $75 000, but that mixes up which amount is the total and which is the factor's multiple.
a.clue: The loan is the repayment times the factor.

b.q: Tom borrows $25 000 and repays it in 12 equal monthly repayments at 1% per month. The table factor is 11.2551. What is each repayment, to the nearest cent?
b.why: Repayment = 25 000 ÷ 11.2551 = $2221.22. Dividing by 12 gives $2083.33, but that ignores interest, so it is too low. Adding a flat 1% of the loan to that gives $2333.33, which is not how the table works.
b.clue: Divide the loan by the factor. Interest is already built into the factor.

check.summary: No problems found. The factor 11.2551 and both repayments ($888.49 and $2221.22) check out, and each question has exactly one right option.
